items.text: The concept of God is realized through the Guru.
'Guru' is a special state of existence that observes and acts upon the karmas across eons and the karmic traditions of each era.
Only a soul that has taken millions of births and thirsted solely for wisdom can realize the word of Brahman.

The space is self-luminous. One must see the Guru in that self-luminosity. Through that, one can perceive the extent of the Guru's potential. This is the principle. Vedantins, researchers, and psychologists have no role to play here.
Among individuals, the one I love the most is my spiritual Guru, Hureshia Fakir.
A Guru must be one who has assimilated all the special powers of divine nature. The path of gods and goddesses is not meant for us to follow.
The religion I believe in is one of friendship. It is of brotherhood and of truth.

What is the magnitude of the title 'Guru'? The inevitability of the Guru arises at the stage where the meritorious essence of the soul and the physical duties must be corrected and guided. That constitutes the profoundness of the enigma called Guru.
The term 'Guru' does not refer to someone who acquires knowledge. A Guru is one who has, over a long period, observed and managed the evolutionary process of the soul.
The state of being a Guru is equivalent to God.
If the word 'Guru' denotes a supernatural power ordained by nature, it cannot be comprehended through written Vedas or poetry.
Nothing meant to understand the Guru has been written down anywhere.
The Guru can only be known through experience.
God is the same for everyone, everywhere. The Guru is the doorway to that ultimate goal.
You must not become isolated. It is my desire that you should live together like the children of one father.

The Guru is the bestower of vision in the atom, in the infinite, and in the deity of worship. He is the one who has attained clarity by witnessing the three times, brings clarity to others, and repeatedly resolves actions.
The difference between a Guru and a deity is immense. A life lived without being able to understand this is futile.
The Guru is a visionary who perceives and dictates what is necessary and what is unnecessary for an era.

The truth of the Guru is the completion of explaining every aspect of knowledge. Or, it is the completion through knowing. Such a truth is the greatness of a soul wherein realization and experiential familiarity merge.
It is a great fortune if we have received an opportunity in this manner (in the state of a Guru) to attain God as ordained by destiny.
The special state of being a Guru is the medium of worship in Santhigiri.
The fundamental mistake we have made is failing to understand the greatness of the Guru.
It is in this era that the entity known as the Guru shines in the world in its complete form.
For those who act with faith in the Guru's words, it is experienced as truth and as God.
The Guru, who is the knower of the three times, is absolute.
The Guru is the embodiment of all dharmas and the epitome of all fortunes.
To the brothers and sisters who consider attaining human birth as a curse, I have only one thing to say. I am prepared to impart my power to you.
The world should not know me as a Siddha, a sorcerer, or a Vedic priest.
Once the supreme light, which is more glorious than all other lights, is extinguished in the lineage, I shall no longer remain.
In the Kali Yuga, deities have no place. In Kali, the place belongs to the Guru. The devotee's place is on the Guru's lap. And the Guru's place is in the devotee's heart.
In order to instil courage in you, the brave souls of karma who have attained a perfectly worthy birth, I am trying to reveal myself before you. You may be convinced by this.
There is a realm beyond billions of solar systems. It is a plane where everything has merged, and nothing more remains to merge into it. The Guru is the one who fulfills that dharma.
If one finds a Guru, they will be able to attain spiritual merit at least equivalent to the fortune of their soul.
The fulfillment obtained through the grace of the Guru, which is attained by means of surrender, cannot be achieved no matter how much sacrifice one performs.
Everyone is equal before the Guru.
Guru is the glory of a tradition that perceives and acts upon everything.
"Great sages praise what they witness day by day." That represents the visionary Guru.
The Guru is the glory of time.
Whatever the disciple is entitled to will come to them. The Guru will not ask whether you have done this or seen that. This is the merit of a Guru.
Any evil is destroyed when it is surrendered to the Guru.
The Guru we seek must be capable of voluntarily taking upon himself the karma of the one who approaches him, exactly as it is.
When a disciple advances a little further, he begins to feel that he and the Guru are not different. This realization will pave the way to the soul of truth.
The Guru can transform the karmic residue only by repeatedly making the disciple perform actions.
You should never feel that I have departed from you. You must not think that I do not exist. I am not different from you. I stand as everything in everyone.
I stand as a white light beyond imagination.
The Guru and the disciple represent the karmic purity that transforms the prana, the vital force, and the soul into the Supreme Soul.
In the end, when there is no one to accompany a person, the only entity that will come with him is the truth known as the Guru.
May God bless you. I desire that the power of Brahman may bestow grace upon you.

A single moment is enough for the Guru-disciple bond to occur. The Guru will not have to speak pointlessly to them. That is how the destined attainment of the Guru and the rightful disciple materialize.
After three hundred and fifty years, you must be careful. Not just in Kerala, but through children born in any part of the world, this ideology will come to the forefront.
Only a visionary who is a knower of the three times and can perceive the eras can save you.
The Guru works to bring about transformation in society during specific periods.
Understand the announcements of yesterday, the happenings of today, and the consequences of tomorrow through Guru Dharma.
My duty is to inform the world, through ordinary and ignorant people like you, how Kali Dharma, the greatest correction to the Manu system, should be established as Brahman in the world.
The knowledge recorded thus far indicates that a system has been ordained for a better tomorrow for the world by flawlessly preserving the respective dharma of each era for humanity.
The Guru is the gateway to the ultimate goal.

The Guru is the dharma that has manifested according to the divine will of Brahman, in order to proclaim the dharma of Kali Yuga and mould the custodians of karma who are destined to become pure souls.
I am doing nothing of my own. I am merely an instrument.

If it were just for me to survive, there would be no need to struggle so much. I could just wear a loincloth, sit quietly as a Swami, and everyone would take care of my needs. But I prefer to live as one among you.

"The lamp that shines forth upon the dissolution of the triad (Triputi) cannot be grasped by a fake ascetic"—a fake ascetic is one who justifies himself by denying the karmic trajectory that has existed until now.
The Guru-disciple relationship brings wakefulness, dreams, and visions down to earth and corrects their state transitions in manifold ways.
The Guru is meant to alter the karmic trajectory of previous births.
I do not have paths like Siddhi to offer. Siddhi has never improved anyone. Nor has it improved the land.
Gurus were appointed here and there with the thought that at least some dharma should prevail among humans.
The attainment of a Guru will be the opening of the door to realize what constitutes the righteous and unrighteous actions you perform.
I am someone who has come to do the work assigned by God. If you wish to partake in that work, you may do so. If not, don't.

People of all religious doctrines stand within the fold of Guru Dharma. The dharma of the Guru, which is capable of illuminating all doctrines, is what is meant by the phrase 'Guru is the soul of all dharmas'.
The desire of a perfect Guru is to reform everyone.
Guru Dharma is infinite and immeasurable.

By invoking Vedic dharma to deny Guru Dharma, or acting in a state of ignorance where dharma is obscured without understanding the greatness of prophetic dharma—the orchestrators of this ignorance are trying to escape by performing Tantric rituals and incantations. This is my experience. This is what I have seen.

The purpose of Brahman is to reveal a life revered by the Guru and disciple, which is enveloped in consciousness and is unitive in nature. It is the path of liberation of Santhigiri, ordained by Brahman. The truth of truth, the source of fulfillment. The pure, brilliant intellect.

The karma I am making you perform is one that elevates them to a great state by rectifying the flaws in the tradition of deities and sages that has come down from the beginning to the present day, ensuring that the karma in those traditions is not broken. What, then, should be your stature!

A Guru is not someone who displays miracles. What you need is to cultivate humility and be guided towards good fortune. This should grow and be passed down through generations. This is what it is meant for.
Love for the Guru must be expressed through humility. Things unfold in the world according to the course of karma, and that truth is realized through the Guru.
No one should wish to blindly believe in anything, stand divided, and move towards the path of self-destruction.
The Guru-disciple relationship means acting with a true understanding of the Guru.
The physical body itself serves as the foundation for spirituality. The essence of spirituality arrives on its own, whether one is aware of it or not.
God has provided us with this path (Gurumargam) to bring the efforts of the great souls to fruition.
Our purpose in visiting sacred places must be to acquire the spiritual merit necessary to transform our very lives.
Within the lineage of the Guru, one must not harbor thoughts regarding caste, religion, or class.
One must ensure that the staff of resolve does not break. If it breaks, everything is lost. This is because resolve is what serves as the foundational support.
My path is in accordance with the divine will.
It is entirely sufficient simply to never violate the words of the Guru; that encompasses everything.
The Guru's path is the most superior. The Guru's path is capable of forging a cultural heritage that will endure for hundreds of thousands of years.
You must not force the children growing up before you into the outdated knowledge of the past in which you were raised.
Move forward through righteous deeds. Find atonement for your sins. To achieve this, seek the guidance of the Gurus.

This concept does not originate from me; consider me merely as an instrument. Whether commanded by the Guru or acting voluntarily in the absence of a command, a Brahmachari must constantly strive in their studies and in serving the Guru. Both of these constitute the fundamental duties of a disciple.
Disobeying the words of the Guru will pave the way to destruction.
The karma accumulated over countless lifetimes across our many past incarnations remains deeply intertwined and ingrained within this current life.
Even if one places their faith in the truth of the Guru, errors will still occur if they lack the discernment to understand what must be strictly followed and comprehended.
There exists a divine grace bestowed by God here (at Santhigiri). It is not exclusively meant for any single caste, religion, or sect.
Distinctions based on religion, caste, and class must never arise within this lineage. If anyone behaves in such a manner, I will manifest as a formidable force and destroy everything.
Strive to embrace the ultimate truth without denying it through arguments of its existence or non-existence.

The Guru must never be given cause to be angry with the disciples. What should be the true nature of a disciple's dedication? It is the realization that whatever actions one performs, they are entirely for the Guru. With this profound sense of dedication, one must perceive all the divine attributes of God within the Guru.

There are two paths to worship God: the path of deities and the path of the sage lineage. The era of the deities' prominence was during the Treta Yuga and Dvapara Yuga. The path of the Guru exists so that humanity can exhaust, through subsequent births, the consequences of the mistakes committed across various eras.
If humility leads one to truth, then truth will lead one to the Guru. The Guru will, in turn, lead one to God.
Do not assume that you can believe in the Guru simply by understanding him on your own. You can only begin to believe by bringing him into your thoughts through gradual familiarity.
Do not assume that the Gurus can be truly understood merely by reading what is written on paper.
You are all active practitioners of the truth. You must deeply desire and actively strive to become exactly that.

God has not given us any deficiency that requires us to bow before anyone. Dispassion represents the strength to forgive and endure everything. The humility to dedicate all forms of dispassion towards a single ultimate goal is our greatest ornament.
One must be able to obey the Guru's words with a profound sense of duty.
All my affairs must be communicated to everyone, and everyone must execute them collectively.

We have initiated the effort here to embrace the sacrifice inherent in this ideal. For this purpose, God has provided us with a path. We must follow that path. Regardless, the world is in absolute need of a course correction.

God has inherently granted us the opportunity to reclaim the fragments that the world has lost. If we fail to set this right, it will be lost once again. These fragments must be nurtured to serve as the support and shelter for the divine will.

The path of the Guru advised at Santhigiri is the ultimate method of liberation. It operates the branches of dharma—spanning from the microscopic atom to the infinite universe—through every individual, bringing it back to their very core. This ensures that the righteous life, which must be achieved through vigilant adherence to divine commands, eradicating sorrow, accumulating merit through action, and preserving dharma as its foundation, reaches not just humanity but all living beings.
Let us eternally share the pure blessedness experienced and the pain endured in revealing the truth across different eras and through a life of dharma.

Your true resolve lies in firmly maintaining the awareness of truth, no matter what you may lose. That is your core duty, and that is the truth that must be elevated within you. Prepare yourselves for this very truth.

By perceiving everything in the position of the Guru and seeing it contained within the Guru, one must adopt the Guru's perspective as stated by the author of the Gita (Lord Sri Krishna Paramatman): 'The Guru is the soul of all dharmas'.
Whether the great souls came for their own sake or for the sake of the world, their true purpose was the execution of the divine will.
The simplicity of the disciple lies in observing how the gross, the subtle, and the law of cause and effect—which exist beyond ordinary thought—have historically operated throughout all times.

Those who perform miracles are entirely ignorant of the dharma of the era. They merely revolve within the vast collections of texts written by both scholars and laymen under the guise of the philosophy of dharma.

Numerous great individuals have toiled arduously to highlight both the external and internal aspects of the ascetic practices of the sages who have appeared in the world thus far. This is exactly what the Hindu religion and the prophet-hood born of divine conception must demonstrate.
No one can ever sever the cycle of karma except through the sacred dharma of the Guru-disciple relationship.

Upon witnessing the fulfillment of the three states of consciousness—waking, dreaming, and deep sleep—one must entrust the untying of the knots leading to the fourth state (Turiya) to the Guru. When the Guru unties these knots, the life of the disciple attains absolute freedom. This is true liberation.

It vividly demonstrates the true nature of the benevolent and malevolent deities, ancestors, sages, and ascetics worshipped by our forebears. This is the essence of the Guru Pooja performed at Santhigiri.

The Guru Pooja conducted at Santhigiri is a divinely ordained ritual that identifies and unravels the karmas accumulated over countless past lifetimes, ultimately elevating the individual to a state equivalent to that of a deity or a sage.
Grounded in monotheistic faith, the Guru Pooja at Santhigiri serves as the foundation stone of spiritual action that unties the knots of karma accumulated across numerous lifetimes.

By completely eliminating the destruction of devotees inherent in the dharma of changing eras, and by demonstrating what true devotion and wisdom entail, the Guru Pooja at Santhigiri is a ritual that grants liberation by illuminating the steps toward the Age of Truth (Satya Yuga).

Innumerable forms of Guru Poojas, Deva Poojas, and Pitru Poojas are conducted across India. The Guru Pooja at Santhigiri is performed to eliminate the obstacles faced by those destined to live as Brahmacharis, householders, or ascetics in the Kali Yuga, ensuring they attain greatness in their respective paths of life.
The Guru Pooja at Santhigiri is a sacred action aimed at rescuing millions from every form of deviation and guaranteeing them the opportunity for salvation and liberation, which are divine gifts.

If a virtuous son or daughter is born, we can purify our lineage through them. The purification of the lineage is not merely for our own sake, but for the purification of our nation and our entire clan. This is the ultimate purpose of Guru Pooja.
What is performed at Santhigiri under the name of Guru Pooja is, in reality, Rishi Pooja. A Rishi represents the Guru across the ages.
You casually claim that there is a supreme power ruling over this world, but do you speak with any true knowledge of that power?

The worship of God exists in every doctrine. That is, even if one worships a demon, we invoke it by crying out, "Oh God!" The worship of God is a knowledge that must be practiced with righteous understanding.
If the God for me and the God for you are two different entities, then what is the significance?
The primordial knowledge must be obtained by us absolutely and directly from God Himself.
The methodology of Santhigiri is to instruct us on how to worship God in accordance with our capacities and our level of attainment.
Humanity has never been able to fully perceive the glory of God, nor carefully understand or study its magnitude and the centers of divine wisdom.
We must establish our testimony in a singular 'One'. Moreover, that testimony must rationally and clearly exist before us.

When speaking of the love for God, one must envision a form for God in the mind. This is because God indeed has a form. Otherwise, if we simply say that God is omnipresent and attribute various other meanings, we will never be able to understand God.
Although God is formless, He possesses an intrinsic form.
A person does not attain divine knowledge merely through calculations that measure everything from the atom to the infinite universe.
For us living in this world to stand united, a unifying 'one' is necessary. Rooted within that 'one', it must pervade everything. That 'one' is the ultimate truth.
The greatness of creation lies in the fact that the glory of God is infused in all living beings.

Behold the forests filled with stones and thorns as a beautiful garden. Through the experience of visiting such a place, one will enjoy the entire beauty of the world. Through that, one might even envision God. Such a fulfilled mind to see God in everything can be termed in a single word as supreme wisdom.
A person who desires the love of God may have to experience overwhelming sorrows either from the deity or from the Guru they believe in.
To be favored by fortune, one must first pray to God, followed by the efforts required for our survival.
Defying the word of God is what constitutes the demonic nature. It was that demonic nature which led Adam astray.
The diverse historical truth of the nine planets is what sustains a single life. It cannot be proven through the prowess of knowledge measured merely by intellect.
Whatever we ask, we will receive an answer from God.
The love or medium that is God is the truth. It is love, it is glory, and it is simplicity.
God always cherishes the devotee, much like a mother who does not let her child cry.
God makes us perform minor deeds and in return grants us magnificent rewards.
It is for the grace of God that we must engage in divine worship.
God has provided you with so many paths in so many places. Yet, you do not embrace them.
Do not seek to acquire merit by destroying all the virtues of life and trying to convince the world through speaking, singing, and writing all the knowledge you have learned.
You do not need to do anything for God. What is required is to experience the sorrow of the heart and reap the fruits of that pain.
It is God who searches for and guides each soul.

God leads us on a path where, after teaching us how to refine and use food and clothing and how to lead our lives, our intellect is directed towards spiritual contemplation, making us worthy of the liberation of the soul.
If the perfect model of divine love, respect, and humility reaches you, it can be utilized for the benefit of the land and its people.
What you ought to receive is the merit of your actions. That must first be obtained from God. You should consider that calling upon God is not for God's sake, but for your own.
You are the ones who must listen to and understand the word of God, and act by immersing yourselves in it. You are not meant to act with petty intellects, fall here and there, and decay.
There are mystical powers as well as many sleight-of-hand tricks. Believing in any of these is not true faith in God at all. Is God supposed to show us magical powers?
Suppose a person receives money as soon as he prays. Is God supposed to just ruin him completely?
God resides exactly where science reaches its limits and halts.
God cannot manifest in a manner where there is a different God for every caste.

What is the special virtue of the intellect that thinks one can gain favors by offering vows and gifts to God? Such individuals can neither respect the duties of the time nor attain self-acquired spiritual merit.
You will not attain God's love through your status and foolishness. You must not lead your life in a way that makes it absolutely impossible to undertake the divine duty.
We must not discard what God gives us. Whatever God provides is beneficial for all of you.
God is the same everywhere and for everyone.
God does not reside where a few rationalists, salvation-seekers, scholars, and intellectuals sit together and establish arguments through debate.
Even if you are cut to pieces inch by inch, you must remain steadfast in God.
Because we are unable to revere God through love, we resort to telling stories about everything.
The words of God are mysterious. Simply acting in accordance with those words will bring you everything.
As long as there is life, there is no substitute for the determination that one will find a personality who understands the duties of the era and makes one worthy of realization.
There is one thing; God has given a sphere that is accessible to anyone among you.
In this world, whether it is great personalities or living beings, no two are exactly alike. That is the glory of God.
Do not say 'Aham Brahmasmi' (I am Brahman). We are not Brahman. We are merely a fraction of Brahman.
The changes in time and the duties of the era are the will of God.
The controller of this universe stands adorning this entire nature. Innumerable great souls born out of the purity of that power's intention remain as spheres of light in the atmosphere.
The permanent resolution to the accumulated actions we have performed knowingly or unknowingly until today - that is the supreme power called God.
We perceive that there is a power in this world beyond our human capabilities. We must believe in that power.
The words that convey the will of God to us are our weapons.
Let us act by surrendering ourselves completely to Brahman.
Those who have attained the vision of Brahman are not bound by actions. One who has not gained that vision attains the cycle of worldly existence in the form of birth and death.
The knower of Brahman leaves his spiritual merit to his disciples and merges into the eternal Brahman through the practice of meditation.
There was a time when the world lacked an understanding of the divine will or the glory of God. It does not mean that this knowledge is complete even now.
The objective of birth should be to uphold the will of God, who is the master of all those who are born and die across ages, not just the spiritually meritorious of many eras.
Brahman has bestowed upon us a much greater capacity to work towards the fulfillment of the era's duties according to the divine will, compared to what others have demonstrated.
None of this was established by me. It is the work done by God to show what divine glory is among you.
If one disregards the will of God, danger lurks both ahead and behind.
Krishna (Supreme Soul Sri Krishna) was born as the eighth son in the eighth state. It was also proven that it is the face of wisdom.
If one considers around twenty-five historical figures, the Prophet is a great one among them. It was the Prophet, who attained Samadhi in the sixth state, who said that Jinn rule the world.
A person who completes 70,748 visions becomes worthy of the divine presence.
Santhigiri's approach is not Vedanta or anything else. Everyone should receive everything.
Once the soul merges into Brahman, there is no more activity. There are no joys or sorrows. It is a state of absolute dissolution.
No one can bring forth a new doctrine and simply pluck away the will of God.
We must engage in divine worship for the grace of God.
If humanity has a certain truthfulness, each realm has its own truthfulness. That belongs to God.
We must take only the path given by God. Do not take any other path. Taking another path will lead to harm.
What is that 'one' which remains innumerable even if counted one by one exhaustively? What meaning do you attribute to it?
You do not need to do anything for God. What is necessary is to act with a sorrowful heart and reap the fruits of that pain.
God does not insist that He must be worshipped. If you do worship, at least do not distort it.

For what purpose does the society generally conduct divine worship today? Why do people go to places of worship and ashrams? It merely ends up with breaking coconuts and lighting lamps for very trivial, immediate gains. The state upon returning is even worse than when they went.
Until now, we have been behaving by standing behind a passed-down tradition where there is a minor God for minor castes and a major God for major castes.
You should be prepared to grasp all kinds of divine blessings from God. That shall be your duty.
It is not that nothing exists. Thinking in that manner will lead to emptiness.
Prayer can bring about goodness to us, our society, and the entire living world. It must be performed with the conceptualization of the Divine.
I have no doubt that your prayers will provide support and shelter to the world.
What we must do is to firmly acquire what we have received through powerful prayer. Through that prayer, the baseness of this world can be wiped away.
A devotee can express all his emotions and sorrows to God through prayer with a sense of surrender. From this, peace is obtained.

There should be a firm belief that the negative effects of our ancestors can be eliminated through prayer; this prayer will certainly succeed in destroying sinful forces and bringing about virtuous merits.
When our chanting of the holy name spreads, through the resolve within it, all baseness will catch fire and perish from the subtle energy of the universe.
This unbroken chanting (Akhandanamajapam) is what we received to remove the obstacles we faced when we worshipped gods and goddesses.
I am once again reminding you of the 1987 birthday message. If we are not to wander for drinking water and food, we must pray to the one God without going after deities and sub-deities.

Our distress has ended. We wish to see the birth of a qualified manhood for the recognition of the home, the sustenance of the nation, and the good of the world. O Father, please make this a reality as God. That salvation is the growth through a lineage of Gurus.
The heartfelt experience you have received is enough in itself. You must pray that this heartfelt experience remains helpful until the very end.
Without wasting the time we have been given, let us, the learned and the unlearned together, earnestly pray to God with active dedication to fulfill the dharma of this age.

The fourth quarter of the four yugas is Kali. We were taught that it is bad, and it was written off as destruction. The notion that all people born in the Kali Yuga are afflicted by Kali is incorrect.
You cry when pain comes. You must pray that even through that crying, you may be able to do His will.
We must pray intensely and attain it. Let prayer be our fervent supplication.
Our prayer is intended to remove all the harms that have occurred in this world due to worship, and to cleanse the evil in the corrupted souls so that they may attain a birth grounded in goodness.
Changing the nature of prayer and the nature of worship is the solution to natural disasters.
Pray earnestly to God, and change will come to you.
First, pray for the eradication of all the impurities that have existed in our minds to date, and for the fruits of that action to belong to all of us.
When you cook food, when you serve it, and whatever you do, you must do it while praying for this ego to be destroyed.
For fortune to favor us, we must first pray to God. Following that is the action for our survival.
The foundational nature of everything in our ashram has come through prayer. A state will emerge where the world understands what our prayer is for.
Santhigiri has revealed everything about all the glories that have manifested in the world, and about all the past Acharyas and their incarnations.
Ensure that everyone is anchored in the true realization of God, rather than being fixed in the tantric practices seen today.
We must reflect on where we stand today in the actions of worshipping and causing others to worship.
Devotion is like a great mountain of love. It is also a path of love.
Devotion is the perfection of love.
Once devotion comes, one should not jump into action showing only initial enthusiasm.
A true devotee joyfully perceives the form of his beloved deity in all moving and non-moving beings.
As devotion increases, there will be a soothing coolness in loving.
When one becomes a devotee, an inquiring nature is inherent in them, even if they lack knowledge.
Becoming an authority on liberation is a void concept. Only Brahman is the authority. The merging of the soul will also be in it. With that comes liberation.
Nothing can be completed without devotion.
If a path of fulfillment is to emerge through the actions you all perform together, you must also reflect on how it should be done.
If one is a devotee, there is no sense of "I". He will surrender everything to the Guru.

Our ancestors are the ones who gave us the story of the eighteen-handed Mother Bhadrakali, and the story of Ghatotkacha traveling through the sky in his heroic valor and showering snakes upon our heads.
A human value emerged through the lives of our sacrificing ancestors. We too can acquire that value only through a life of sacrifice.
The Mahatmas are those who bathed at four o'clock when the melting snow flowed in the river Ganges, and engaged in painful chanting and penance.
We are not willing to emulate the goodness that our ancestors demonstrated through their lives of sacrifice. What we see today is the light of their long periods of suffering.
India is a land where many Mahatmas were born. They endured great hardships to create and uphold justice. They nurtured it to great heights and imparted it to the kings.
He who needs to be beaten must be beaten, and he who needs to be killed must be killed. Sri Krishna did exactly that.
The birth of Krishna became necessary when actions reached a point where they were shrouded in stories, sung, narrated, and turned into mere theatrical plays.
Our beginning is from where Narayana Guru, Buddha, and Krishna left off.
The wise ones (Jnanis) perform the very same subjects that the sages (Rishis) bring to completion.
Only if beings like Jesus, the Prophet, or other such Mahatmas are born among the people of today's generation can actions appropriate for the times be brought about.
In Kali Yuga, the mission of the Mahatmas is to impart true knowledge, sacrifice, and purity of action to the Shudra class in general, and to the believing public in particular.
Mahatmas are the mediums through which one can love truth and understand actions with distinct clarity.
Theories insist that a Mahatma should be born as a king of kings; however, if one asks what the logic behind that theory is, we mostly see an operational capacity that is left speechless.

The first requirement is the eradication of ignorance. Only that will lead to success. What is needed for that? We must understand the life vision of the great ones. We must reflect upon it. Then, we should strive to put it into practice. If we try step by step in this manner, we can reach our intended destination.
The Guru, who is the truth of truths, is the Lord of the world who showers compassion upon the presence of God, the presence of the Deity, the presence of Brahman, and the presence of Parabrahman.
What we see through history and observation is that no Mahatma ever received due recognition in their own homeland.

Our life's goal should be to emulate, in the atom and the infinite, the brilliant sacrifices of the past prophets who shared their great lives or completed them wrestling with body and soul, and the eminent sages who shared their lives for us, thereby completing the course of dharma known as the gross, subtle, and causal realms.
If one can offer the sacrifice, love, and respect of the wise and the realized, then each person becomes a special manifestation of dharma that reveals the truth.
Simply evaluating, criticizing, or justifying past Mahatmas does not mean that the greatness of guidance is complete. The secret of life they discovered must be revealed.

No matter which Acharya appears in which country, their core idea is the same. Today's need is a lineage that encompasses the ideas of all Acharyas. The freedom of that lineage is what will contribute to world peace.
An Acharya is superior to ten Upadhyayas (teachers).

Because of the teaching of the Vedas, an Acharya is called a father. It is because they render a great service equivalent to that of a father that authorities like Manu designate the Acharya as a father. The great service that Acharyas perform is making humanity qualified for Vedic duties.
The physical structure of the Acharyas who came in different eras is unique. Through each individual who came in a distinct structure, specific actions have emerged in their respective times.
World Gurus and their words must be venerable to us.
To be able to see the realms where the life course of our ancestors is stuck, exactly in that form. That is the dharma of direct perception.
The downfall of India began the very day hypocrisy started in the name of Sannyasa.
There is an art to Sannyasa. The art of Sannyasa is full of great merit and love.

Sannyasa is not the act of feeding, nurturing, and destroying people using money, intellect, and logic. You must understand that a "Sannyasi" means "completely blessed." Knowledge, wealth, and mastery will all reach the place where he sits.
Sannyasa is not retreating into some corner to sever oneself from actions, like closing one's eyes to create darkness.
Sannyasa is needed within our homes and in our minds.
Sannyasa is the light of God.
Sannyasa is not going to lie down and die in some wayside shelter when one is perishing without the means to eat and drink.
Living a life of uselessness to one's home and society, only to ultimately don saffron robes, does not constitute *Sannyasa*; it is rather a thoroughly fourth-rate mockery.

The counterfeit practices of royal sages (*Rajarshis*), who supposedly sat atop trees without even drinking water while listening to tales, have been implemented here under the guise of *Sannyasa*. It is a profoundly toxic tradition.
Retreating to the forest does not signify *Sannyasa* at all. *Sannyasa* must be cultivated in a manner befitting the contemporary era.
The fundamental duty (*Karma*) of a *Sannyasin* is to address and resolve the problems of society.
The sacrifice of a *Sannyasin* yields absolute fulfillment in any endeavor. An awareness of this truth will bestow fortune and prosperity upon your progeny.
A *Sannyasin* achieves ultimate realization solely through their diligent effort and sacrifice.

The body is meant for the performance of duty (*Karma*); even the worship of the Divine is a form of *Karma*. Consequently, the foremost duty of a *Sannyasin* is to address the issues afflicting society.
A *Sannyasin* possesses esoteric knowledge that renders the body immune to venom, regardless of whether the bite is from a king cobra or any other highly venomous serpent.
Those who are designated as *Sannyasins* are inherently pure and sanctified from birth.
A *Sannyasin* in action may deviate from traditional rituals. However, if their dutiful action (*Karma*) is not meticulously preserved, everything is ultimately lost.
When the sacrifice of a *Sannyasin* is duly honored, the resultant spiritual benefits accrue to the householders (*Grihasthas*).
*Sannyasins* must abstain from exhibiting occult powers (*Siddhis*).

There is a widespread misconception that a *Sannyasin* is one who desires nothing, wanders aimlessly, is a mere beggar, or a mendicant. This is fallacious. One must perceive and comprehend a *Sannyasin* as the embodiment of all righteousness (*Sakala Dharmatma*).
Celibacy (*Brahmacharya*) represents the most profoundly truthful dimension of human existence; this innate truthfulness must be consciously cultivated.
The ignorance of exhibiting affection toward a *Sannyasin* on the basis of communal affiliations will inevitably invite destruction.
The fundamental objective of *Brahmacharya* is the thorough study and comprehension of the state of one's own household, society, and nation.
Comprehending vision (*Darshana*) solely through intellectual reasoning inevitably leads to errors; if it merely develops within the intellect, absolute clarity remains elusive.

*Darshana* is the process of illumination and rectification that occurs when the ascetic practices (*Tapas*), which elevate the soul to a state of sanctity, harmoniously reveal both past errors and righteous deeds.
*Darshana* fundamentally signifies the realization of the Ultimate Truth (*Sat*) through the discerning comprehension of both good and evil.
A comprehensive and detailed perception of Nature requires the realization of 7444 philosophical visions (*Darshanas*).
A true visionary (*Dirghadarshi*) is one who possesses the insight to perceive the inner workings of the solar system.

Rather than exploring distant celestial bodies or engaging in actions that degrade humanity, a visionary initially dedicates themselves to deciphering the magnitude and profound significance of an action (*Karma*) within this very solar system.

The concepts of visionary foresight (*Dirgha Darshana*), the path of devotion (*Bhakti Darshana*), yogic discipline (*Yoga Darshana*), righteous action (*Karma Darshana*), and ethical duty (*Dharma Darshana*) encompass thousands of avenues for self-realization and spiritual insight.

*Darshana* is not an oscillating state of action that oscillates between observing existence and non-existence. Rather, true *Darshana* is the unwavering perception solely of that which inherently exists.

What is the act of *Darshana*? *Darshana* constitutes a profound dialogue between a Guru and a disciple, founded upon the discerning comprehension of shifting paradigms such as cause, effect, spatial context, and subtlety. It serves as a collaborative refinement of knowledge between the preceptor and the student. It is explicitly not an abstract theoretical framework that nullifies righteous action (*Karma*) under the pretext of mere revelations and realizations.

*Grihasthashrama* is the profound duty wherein one's entire life—endowed with wealth, knowledge, and prosperity—becomes capable of instructing even the nations of the world, should the necessity arise.

Householders must not only strive relentlessly for the welfare of their offspring but also diligently safeguard their spiritual lineage. In this context, lineage refers specifically to the unbroken succession of spiritual preceptors (*Guru Parampara*).
Householders are in no manner destined for degradation. Through their very existence, they are meant to systematically acquire and manage wealth, profound knowledge, and enduring prosperity.
Individuals abiding in the householder stage must execute their inherent duties with unwavering commitment.
A householder must adhere to a highly disciplined lifestyle, consciously cultivating the expertise and persistent effort required to raise their children in the most exemplary manner possible.

Irrespective of the adversities faced, a householder must possess an unyielding resolve, asserting, "I shall endure any hardship for the sake of my lineage; I am prepared to make any sacrifice necessary to cultivate the next generation."

The ascetic (*Sannyasin*) and the devotee both invariably emerge from the fold of householders. Consequently, it is the householders who must attain paramount excellence, as their role is unequivocally foundational.
Should householders unite with shared intent and concerted action, malevolence would be entirely eradicated from the face of the earth.
In autonomously executing the righteous duties (*Dharma*) of a householder, you are, in reality, experiencing absolute and unadulterated freedom.

Rather than reveling in the recurrent narration of obsolete and worn-out tales, householders must strive to become warriors of righteousness (*Dharma Yoddhas*), capable of instilling the profound courage of dutiful action (*Karma*).

A householder is bound by five primary duties: duty toward ancestors (*Pitri Dharma*), duty toward the household (*Griha Dharma*), duty toward the divine (*Deva Dharma*), the duty of charity (*Dana Dharma*), and the duty toward the self (*Atma Dharma*). How does one attain mastery and authority over these five quintessential duties?
Life is essentially a contemporary narrative fraught with immense tribulation, paradoxically concealed beneath the lexicon of joy.
Life constitutes an intricate matrix of knowledge, meticulously acquired through relentless quests and profound experiences oriented toward the attainment of comfort and security.
Disentangling the complex web of life is as impossibly daunting a task as untying the intricate knots of a meticulously woven spiderweb.
Life is, in essence, the soul's continuous recitation of the sacred Vedas.

There exists no individual devoid of the desire to attain goodness. Just as the amalgamation of a specific element into the nine quintessential minerals (*Navapashanas*) transmutes them into gold, and a subsequent refinement yields pure gold, life must be similarly elevated to unalloyed purity through the assimilation of essential virtues.
Among all incarnations, a human birth is universally regarded as the most supreme.
A human existence is profoundly intended for the attainment of supreme spiritual blessedness.
The very privilege of obtaining birth in this mortal realm is an achievement of unparalleled magnitude.
It is profoundly the experiences of suffering and sorrow that meticulously sculpt and mold a human life.
What is it that you truly require? It is the unequivocal purification of your inner soul.
We, as humanity, are the direct descendants of those within the lineage of Manu who engaged in righteous action with an earnest yearning for the Divine presence.

Throughout our existence, we are obligated to comprehend the virtues and vices of bygone eras. For what underlying reason have these karmic consequences attached themselves to us? This profound inquiry is precisely what life demands us to understand.
One need only realize that we represent a mere infinitesimal speck among an innumerable multitude of atoms. Furthermore, we bear an inexhaustible historical legacy of karmic transgressions.
The adversities we endure are fundamentally not for our own individual existence; rather, they serve as a foundation for the sustenance and prosperity of subsequent generations.
Is it conceivably possible to subsequently reclaim a precious moment of life that was irrevocably lost to a distorted and undisciplined existence?
Our mode of existence is inevitably circumscribed and determined by the intrinsic *Karma* and *Dharma* of the parents we are born to.
The ultimate purpose of human existence transcends the mere intellectual resolution of the mind's transient doubts.

For what purpose were we born, for what reason do we exist, and why are we destined to perish? If our objective is not to unravel this profound enigma, why then should we seek refuge in philosophical declarations of Vedanta that merely exude an external aura of purity?

What exactly constitutes our existential reality? It is the dynamic convergence of the five senses, the five primordial elements, the five fundamental sheaths (*Panchakoshas*), and the nine vital consciousnesses that operate both covertly and overtly as the life force and soul. The holistic potency inherent in this collective synthesis is fundamentally embedded within us.
The profound essence of each of our individual lives is intrinsically linked to the cumulative reckoning of a multitude of previous incarnations.

One must rigorously seek spiritual merit (*Punya*) through righteous action (*Karma*), and subsequently pursue auspicious fortune through that acquired merit. Such divine fortune ultimately establishes the foundation for all earthly and spiritual endeavors.

It is not imperative that you embrace *Sannyasa*; rather, what is fundamentally required is the practical wisdom and competence to navigate life. To actualize this, the foremost prerequisite is the spiritual purification of one's ancestral lineage (*Pitri Shuddhi*).
The ultimate objective of our life achieves realization only upon the steadfast adoption and implementation of a highly systematized and disciplined path.

One must undertake a daily and diligent endeavor to transform one's mental disposition. Furthermore, it is imperative to translate this internal transformation into practical action to the maximum possible extent.

While intellectual engagement with Vedanta is permissible, the practical reality of life supersedes it in importance. What precisely constitutes life? In what manner ought one to conduct their existence? These are imperatives that we must profoundly comprehend.
Relinquishing the animosity born of mutual antagonism, one must actively cultivate an unwavering resolve dedicated to mutual affection, compassionate assistance, and collaborative cooperation.
Unwavering punctuality and dutiful discipline are absolutely mandatory. It is this steadfast discipline that earns profound respect and dignity within society.

Regardless of the identity or the underlying purpose of an individual approaching you, there must exist a genuine eagerness to ascertain their needs; this essential disposition constitutes true humility.

Having comprehensively understood the tragic and arduous histories endured by our ancestors, we are morally obligated to unearth and implement specific righteous strategies (*Dharma*) designed for both their spiritual elevation and our collective welfare.
Our foremost armament is encapsulated in the conviction: "I possess nothing but this humble prayer to offer; I trust entirely in the Divine to orchestrate all things on my behalf."

It is a critical imperative that children be nurtured and guided along the path of righteousness. Such proper upbringing is fundamentally essential for the overarching progress and prosperity of the nation.

It is crucial to meticulously guide the spiritual experiences manifesting in both children and adults, ensuring they progress without error. One must deliberate on how these profound realizations can be optimally utilized for the greater benefit of humanity, and devise robust strategies to perpetually sustain them. The most viable methodologies must be proactively adopted to achieve this end. In this complex endeavor, unconditional love serves as the paramount and indispensable catalyst.

If nothing else can be achieved, one must, at the very least, cultivate a foundational framework of unity and harmonious coexistence among parents and children, thereby ensuring this profound understanding is deeply instilled within the younger generation.

A multitude of grievous errors and missteps have invariably characterized our earthly existence. Consequently, it is incumbent upon us to engage in relentless and concerted efforts to systematically rectify these past transgressions.

Each of us inadvertently harbors a desperate yearning to merely fulfill the base desires of an inferior existence—an existence profoundly compromised by fundamental ignorance, a lack of spiritual maturity, and the regressive conditioning of antiquarian habits.
If one can lead a life, even a small one, there must be a prosperity derived from it.

Certain things that are useful at respective times in the various stages of children's lives must be imparted to them as a guru's advice. Philosophical matters ranging from Kanyadan and Brahmacharya to Savikalpa Samadhi should be explained to them.

Learn by observing those who have learned through life, or obey them. Is that not the path of the guru-disciple relationship? If you learn carefully to this extent, it becomes a means for you to take care of yourself, and for the people of the world to take care of the world.
If the heap of desires collapses, there will be sorrow. Even if it is a compromising devotion, there will be sorrow.
What is required is to live and act with the firm resolve that everything should happen according to the divine will.
Our path is not meant for picking quarrels. If we go to quarrel like that, another quarrel will catch hold of us.
Moderation must be maintained in everything. Along with the increase in devotion, the passion for action also increases.
A devotee who has realized God in various ways will cry out of love. Even if one is not a true devotee, there will be many outbursts of tears.
All of you are the owners of the karma required to possess a life filled with purity.

Upon waking up in the morning, one must think while sitting on the bed itself. What should I make of my home today? After clarifying this and completing the daily chores at home, one must live aiming for the goodness of the movement without wasting even a single minute.
If you live with discipline, you will be able to understand that good and bad come intermingled every day.
If we tie up our parents' ignorance and our life's shortcomings and chase after pleasure, life will only be wasted.
If the karma that is to be realized through life is lost by singing, talking, and writing it away, will the realm of karma emerge?
The father must be a person with a mind as clear as the sky, and the mother one who speaks profound words.
If the father can lead a respectable life, the children will largely follow suit.
The father must be a person who has attained love through absolute faith, karma through love, merit through karma, and fortune through merit.
Should not the father, who is supposed to be the god to his children, at least attain the knowledge to show them God?
The glory of being father, mother, and children exists only if we bestow it. The status we have brought upon saying 'God' is also the same.
The mother is the first guru. The mother must be knowledgeable. If the mother is good, the home is good.
If the mother cannot obey and manage things here, everything will be ruined. It is not enough for only the father to be good.
Only if the mother imparts every essence of goodness will there be room for the children's perfect knowledge and humility.
Even if the mother lacks knowledge, she has immense love for her children within. Love is glory.
For the upliftment of the home to take place, the woman who is the mother, the first guru, must become good. She must become knowledgeable.
No matter what generational defects one may have, half of those defects will be cured by the goodness of the mother.

Purity of karma must be attained without discrimination. From that, knowledge must arise and bring fortune. When fortune arrives, one must not be arrogant or defiant. That should be the merit of the family.
You, as father, mother, and children, are living like symbols of the animalistic nature of a distorted education. Who can reform you, and how?
The men and women growing up here are the ones who must determine the destiny of the world. It is through this sense of dharma that we must become great.

If you are to be the father and mother to your children, you must be able to make them understand what your ancestors were. Instead of that, you should not impose your intellect on them to hide your own impurities.
It is your fortune if you can contribute a small child who is beneficial to the land or the country. Only through that can you be saved from now on.
It is the purity of karma in marital life that creates the environment for the birth of a child who is useful to the home and the land.
Girls and boys must be raised in a manner that serves the goodness of the world.
No matter how worthless they may be, your children should be of help to at least one other person.
Even if one acquires the eight siddhis, without honesty, the family will fall into ruin. Disregarding honor and dishonor, the desire for truth must be maintained.

Even if there is nothing else, at least an understanding to live together in unity as father, mother, and children must be developed and imparted to the children. Let them grow in that understanding, if they can.
I wish to see the divine will working in your children.
If you have only two children, let both be united. If you have ten, let all ten be united.
In all activities where men and women come together, only actions that embrace each other with love and respect should be performed. Thus, the home will attain a place of unity.
Children who are not deserving of merit will never be entitled to fortune.
A mind that denies the word of truth, whether knowingly or unknowingly, whoever it belongs to, will not be useful to him or his family.

Today, an era of hybridization has arrived. Even for humans and a blade of grass, there is hybridization. This is a very serious matter. We must preserve the word of God without letting this spread to our children. God is in your favor.
The home is not going to improve through foolishness or brute force.
The logic that children must suffer the consequences of their karma is a kind of arrogant talk.
How is the home uplifted? Will the home be uplifted merely through ways to get a lot of money?
A new generation will be formed through the character formation of children. For that, let our own home be prepared first.
The husband should know that his wife must be able to understand him, and the wife should know that her husband must be able to understand her.
It is indeed the duty of men to make efforts to rectify the shortcomings of the female gender.
The path of devotion is the most suitable for family life.
As long as self-knowledge does not arise within those who are called wife, husband, and children, what is the meaning in saying they are not good after the children have grown up improperly?
We must always be ready to gain knowledge from God. We should not allow garbage-like thoughts lying on the roadside to enter our minds.
Unite the home, no matter how hard you have to struggle. Through that, unite the land and the country.
Together, the father and mother should mold children who are useful to the world. This is our goal.
Father, mother, and children must try to move forward together. If each of us does not maintain a sense of care, we will never be able to save ourselves.

The children born in our homes are devoid of dharma. This is because the father and mother do not know how to perform actions to acquire merit. Children devoid of dharma are not entitled to attain merit either.
We are raising children to become the owners of a karmic destiny where offspring, imbued with various sins, compete in various ways. How can they embrace the source of love?
Instead of teaching children to repeatedly fulfill a customary practice that imparts love, all we have imparted to them is conflict.
Whatever antics the father and mother display at home, the children will imitate them. This situation has spread throughout the neighborhood and the entire world.

You, as father and mother, may earn what is needed for one generation of your children. Do not earn beyond that. If you earn like that, your children will become attendants of education, wealth, and enlightenment. Thus they will perish. This is the logic of the Westerner or the capitalist.
If the father and mother do not possess experiential merit, the children will not turn out good.
Thinking about the growth of life is an inherent tendency, and this tendency is equally necessary for father, mother, and children.
Every individual must have all appropriate compromises, outpourings of love, and richness of sacrifice.
Every individual must maintain purity and moderation in their own thoughts and actions.
You must be dignified like an emperor and humble like a servant.
Discover the personality that helps you become worthy of realization. Remain equal in enemy and friend, in honor and dishonor, and in praise and blame.
Each one of you should live here only by maintaining honesty in humility, acquiring courage, and not becoming anyone's slave.
The mind must be as expansive as the sky. It must also be as deep as the ocean.
Men and women must take care that their disposition does not turn bad, so that their mind, word, and deed can reach the goal.
No matter how many times and wherever you fail, you must seek again and again.
Remain equal in happiness and sorrow.
Those who are prepared to determine the destiny of the world must become great through their sense of dharma.
Giving something to someone and taking something from someone is a great imagination of the mind.
He who does not grieve over an insult caused by another sleeps comfortably. He wakes up comfortably. He engages in matters comfortably. But the one who insults perishes as a result of danger.
If we are unable to embrace the spiritual side of the sacrificer, we cannot participate in his dharma or take up the aspect of that merit.
It is a fortunate character not to deny or blame anything, regardless of what one feels.
Good thoughts have spread within us. With those thoughts, the impurities inside must be washed away. Only then can it be said that one has lived as a human being.
Have heart-felt compassion for all living beings, just as for humans, without feeling hatred towards not only fellow human beings but any creature.

Have friendliness towards everyone, compassion, patience, absence of arrogance, and a state of mind that remains unshaken in both joy and sorrow. With this much, you will become someone who loves yourself and God.
If one is a devotee, there is no sense of "I". Everything will be dedicated to God.
Act with humility. Do not think that everything else can be smashed and destroyed.
Does anyone respect the words of a drunkard? Does he himself know how to respect his own words? Then how will others respect them?
Detachment is not enmity; it is the reverence of love.
Do not speak any nonsense like rationalism and salvationism; it will not work.
If a mistake occurs in a small matter, one should not use big words.
Humility is the greatest. Obedience is even greater. Competence corresponds to that.
There is a nature among us to deny and reject everything. Do not assume the embodiment of laziness.
God will not come just by completing things through dancing and singing, playing and making others play, jumping and stepping to the rhythm.
'Prathyakshavaham Dharmam' - One must maintain dignity in seeing dharma manifested.
The heart of each of you is a center of knowledge that must impart your purity of character and simplicity to the people and reclaim them from there.
The attitude that only what I do is right is not good for anyone.
Suppose a colleague of yours has a minor shortcoming. Do not make it big by having four
people join together and talk about it with each other.
We, who portray great souls as bad, are many times worse than the bad itself. We are a lineage that has become bad like this.
What dignity are you going to attain through Advaita philosophy?

When man becomes sorrowful, he forgets everything and wanders in search of refuge. In prosperity, he forgets everything. That is a general nature, but he should be able to create a presence of mind that does not waver or remain unfixed in anything.
Humility and competence constitute dignity.
Being competent is a fortune.
The work I do has that much value and weight. It will not enslave another. Our strong dignity is blossoming like that.
Whatever word it may be, if it causes sorrow to others, it is contrary to attaining heaven.
He whose words and mind are pure, and he who protects both of these at all times, attains all the fruits mentioned in Vedanta science.
Even if one is sorrowful oneself, one should not utter words that cause affliction to dharma for him. One should not do or think anything that causes harm to another.
Krishna's words, 'You are not killing anyone. Nor are you causing anyone to be killed,' are self-evident. That word was sufficient for Bhishma to attain salvation.
Through your actions, you can bring all the goodness and all the fortune you need.
One without knowledge cannot expand any action.
If we proceed to act calmly, everything will come to us.
Doing good is also good itself. Every action has its own merit.
All the good beings that have existed in the world are those who have achieved sacrifice through their actions.
One person should do the work of a thousand people. That is how much more work we have to do. If one strives like that for a year, one will get the result of working for a thousand years.
When doing good, there may be unbearable pain. Then, one must hold on without withdrawing from there. If one withdraws, everything is lost with that.
Even if one is only able to act for a moment, it should be done as an offering to God.

If good is done, an opposition to that good will emerge. When doing good, resistance will come. When doing something to stop the resistance, one will also get weary. Thinking that this is the result of having done service, an opportunity should be given to correct it.
If the Guru is made a witness in karma, the Guru will instill devotion in the karma.
Starting from small karma and going to the big is the right way. Whatever the karma is, it must be done purely. We must be careful that the karma we do does not cause difficulty to another.
He who carries together the karma caused to be done with the Guru as witness and the karma mentioned in the horoscope will not understand the Guru's Paramatman.
Without looking at what karma is being done or where it is being done, one should try to earn merit by doing that karma.
One has to decide for oneself what one's own path of karma and path of dharma should be. It cannot be decided by anyone else.
If you know about light, its frequency, and how light dissolves, you can know about your path of karma.
It is not enough to mention the principle of dharma; the principle of karma holds the importance.
It is not enough if you reach the Trimurti path of karma. I have worked so that you reach beyond that. I can only do it for you. Earning it by performing karma is your duty.
This is the opportunity ordained for you by God. If you perform your karma dedicating it to the Guru, it will benefit the world.
The body is meant to perform karma. Even the worship of God is karma.
A small karma done in the ashram can resolve not only one's own negative aspects but also the flaws in the karma performed by ancestors.
We will only get what is due to us from the karma we struggle to perform with love, humility, and respect.
Once karma goes wrong, another birth itself will have to be taken for the fruits of that karma.
Karma is not a clown that wins by arguing whether it exists or not.
You should also comprehend why you have undertaken to take up karma in connection with worldly life.
One without karma means one who has no love or bond with anything.
Everyone should think about how much courage there is in karma. Man's karma and dharma constitute man's greatness.
By voluntarily taking up the karma that God has entrusted to you with great desire, may you emerge into the dharma that is beyond time and space.
Complete the Kali age through penance and knowledge. Penance is the ascetic power derived through karma.
What becomes fruitful in a field where bookish knowledge is of no use is the path of dharma that earns merit through karma.
The householder adherent to dharma, who becomes the master of karma that molds the owners of dharma by bringing knowledge into karma, is entitled to everything.
If each person has a path of karma, that path of karma will exist in his life.
Karma, which is the motivating force for everything, is beyond thought.
I have struggled to prevent the ignorance inherent in the karma of the people of the world from passing down to generations.
What is called karma is that if we move even a little, it falls under karma.
He who serves the Guru until the end of his body truly attains the eternal Brahman.
To reclaim the virtues in karma, guidance appropriate to the yuga is absolutely necessary.

What is the karma suitable for the dharma that we need to attain within our lifetime? What is the weight of sacrifice in that karma? What hardship is there in that sacrifice? How should we experience that hardship? We should at least know this much.
First of all, we should pray once, respect once, respect each other, and reverently undertake karma in the nature of an ashram. Great things can be acquired through that karma.
You should not perform any karma that is going to destroy dharma by realizing ego through humility.
If you lack capability, perform every karma with resolve and prayer. If so, by the capability of God, one can fully build karma that can impart peace to the land, its people, and the world itself.
None of us wishes to perform a karma that causes a harm to ourselves. Then how did we get so much harm? Think about it.
What is called karma is an acquaintance with the flaws of past karma, as well as the present and the future.
We have a duty towards God. Realizing this, we must live with a sense of duty.
You should have a pleading tone within you, saying, "Let me at least put in the effort of an ant."
Shouldn't we reach the state called self-illumination? Can it be achieved just by talking about it? We must strive for it. Only through the karma of effort can one reach that position.
Whatever shortcomings exist in our homes and country, they must be resolved through our intellect and hard work. We should go to the ashram to familiarize ourselves with that noble karma.
Instead of doing evil and reaping evil, everyone should do good and reap good. We need such a righteous war (dharma yuddha).
Our duty is to transform the 'Kali' of Kali Yuga into a human being. That is very difficult.
One may have to hear the scolding of a thousand people. One must endure whatever anyone does. Yet, there should be a determination that "I will complete a karma."

Perform any karma with intention and prayer. If done so, by God's grace, everything becomes complete. Our effort to build a karma that can impart peace to the land, its people, and the world itself will become fruitful.
Envision and dedicate yourselves with the thought that what we are carrying out is world karma.
"After finishing my work, I would also complete the work of others. I never felt any reluctance in doing so.
Each of us should become the masters of the karma that creates everything needed to grow for our comfort, convenience, and the benefit of the land.
First think, then act. Infuse love, humility, and respect into your actions to bring about goodness.
The impurities accumulated by billions of souls over twenty-five Chaturyugas remain stagnant in this atmosphere. The divine grace bestowed by God to remove those impurities exists in Santhigiri.
Do not distort the sense of duty. If that happens, one will not be able to comprehend even to a small extent the immense craving for misdeeds that might befall them.
We must strive until garbage turns into gems. What we need to know is where to anchor that effort.
Reclaiming the Yuga Dharma is our greatest need.
Everything should be moderate. One's behavior towards anyone should be moderate. There must be a firm resolve to behave with a sense of unity at home.
If a mistake occurs in action, it can be corrected through action. If a mistake occurs in words, it cannot be corrected.
The root cause of whatever we are basing our actions on must be found first.
Guidance suitable for the age is essential to reclaim competence in karma. When it is the Kali Yuga, guidance must be given considering its weight and momentum.
Work without power and hold on through sacrifice. That sacrifice is what saves you.
