One must be willing to confess one's own faults.
The current subject before us consists of numerous historical truths lost in the search for the Ultimate Reality, along with many theories considered to be the meaning of this world.
When goodness comes to the soul, financial stability will follow. If there is no goodness in the soul, whatever status is attained, none of it is permanent.
Know that experiential wisdom, rather than hearsay, is true authority.

It has been divided into so many fragments. Who cut and divided the earth into such fragments? When nature became agitated within itself, the earth fragmented. The primary inquiry will be about the reason for this.
The mind is unwilling to let go of latent tendencies. Yet, it is impossible not to align with the truth. That is the cause of pain.
We have only one religion: the religion of liberation. There is no liberation through any other religion. It is not possible. I have nothing to say to those who claim it is possible.
Hinduism is more than just a religion; it is a culture.
I sincerely appeal to those who call Hinduism the Sanatana religion, and to other sister religions. Brothers, please think.
Why do the children, who should adopt the religion of sacrifice, live together in the unity of love, and work for their home, land, and the world, divide themselves in the name of caste and religion?
Is it right to make people fight each other in the name of caste and religion, invoking the names of the Acharyas?
The religious ideologues that have existed thus far will be destroyed by their respective religions themselves.
The error that befell Hinduism is by divine decree. Very few know this.

A guidance for the people of the world. Through that guidance, when caste is separated from caste, religion from religion, and nation from nation, they will be able to act understanding that all this is the completion of an imitation of one entity.
If we delve deeply into religion, we can see that some kind of inconsistency has crept into religious doctrines.
We could not even respect or accept the Acharyas born in Kerala. The reason is caste.
In the history of a thousand years ago, there is no mention of caste existing here.
When speaking of the Shudra class, it refers to the caste fanatics ranging from the ignorant, the despicable, and the vile, all the way to the Chandala.
The term Shudra is not based on caste. There are Shudras among Brahmins, Kshatriyas, and Vaishyas.
The true teaching of the Indian sages is far removed from the Vedic dharma commands that realize caste through karma.
Caste is the most formidable obstacle. Even a sanyasin has not been able to stay away from caste.
Vedanta is the karmic course that has classified even the renunciates into castes.
If we are to know the Gurus, if we are to feel love for them, the caste system that has destroyed us must depart from our midst.
Caste-based struggles can be seen everywhere. No one knows how to think about raising girls properly, other than engaging in such struggles.
Do you not need a thought that is beyond caste, religion, class, and color differences?
Hindu philosophy or culture is very vast and broad. However, everyone has an obligation to reflect on the fact that an error has occurred somewhere within it.
When reflecting on the system of the Manus, it must also be said that the Trimurti system was a shortcut created to prevent people from discovering the primal source nature.
There is a belief among Hindus that if a deity appears, then nothing is impossible. That is not true.
By writing "Amaranirjjaradeva", the Brahmin was transformed into a deity. Through this, the vast majority of the people were turned into asuras.
Are it not the vested interests who created castes and religions in the name of the Acharyas and kept them fenced within it?
In a single home itself, one is a devotee of Vishnu, another of Shiva, another of Subrahmanya, and another of Kali. The situation is such that each worships claiming their own deity is the greatest.

In the statement of the Varna-ashrama system, 'Brahmajnanethi Brahmana' (one who knows Brahman is a Brahmin), there is no caste. There is no religion either. But when we look at the lore across the length and breadth of India, what has become of the primordial lineage of Manu, the first Guru of the world, today?
Our shortcoming is the ignorance born as a result of engaging in highly uncultured worship while remaining divided by caste, religion, and class.
The wise know that even if castes and religions emerge and their ideologies endure for centuries, it is of no great significance.
Sitting and chanting mantras in satyagraha before a god who has been fortified in the name of caste and religion will not yield any result.
Madan, Marutha, and Bhadrakali are our gods. A deity standing adorned with skulls and snakes is our god. How much good will this god do for us?
The scientist is an ignorant fool who boasts of knowledge by spouting various baseless calculations and citing the speed of light.
Without exception, we have handed over all the knowledge we have discovered thus far into the hands of foreigners.
It does not mean that science is not good; science is good if its destructive power is eliminated.

The guidance of science, which has been able to reveal the biological micro-principles of molecules, is indeed great. However, science can do nothing when it comes to observing the potential of action with the help of the five elements in the atmosphere, recognizing the dharma that acts as its cause and effect, and enabling one to adopt that dharma.
There is a place in the middle of the ocean (the Bermuda Triangle) where no science works. It is the work of a demon who possesses divine grace.
We had neither Vedic authority nor religiosity. All we had were poems and stories written by scholars, and that is all there is today.
Scholarship is a process of polishing.
When listening to those without innate aptitude, others too might believe them to be right, ultimately leading everything into despair.

You are the most blessed among the blessed and the wisest among the wise to have received the opportunity to perform actions according to the divine will, evaluating the rights and wrongs that have come and gone over time. This is the greatest of all greatness.
Over-applying human intellect in any matter will lead to destruction.
Intellect should be used moderately and appropriately. To eliminate something, it must be replaced by something else in its place.
How can the karma of the soul proceed there? This is spiritual.
There is a misconception that self-knowledge (Atmavidya) can only be attained by displaying scholarship and numerous qualifications. Wisdom can be reflected at all times.
Nothing occurs without the gross, the subtle, the effect, and the cause.
Our history is a very long story. A history that is as old as the Manvantaras.
As man flows along with emotions, love fades away, ultimately leading to a state of complete uncertainty. What should we do about it?
Blind denial will cause more harm than good. Denial should be accompanied by discrimination between cause and effect.
When distinguishing between right and wrong, there must be enough sacrifice to correct the wrongdoer rather than destroying them.
We have been given a pure time to become authorities capable of sustaining virtue by understanding the course of Dharma across the three periods of time and reclaiming that Dharma.
What is needed is Dharma commensurate with Karma. It is that Dharma which must be sought, found, and knocked open.
What you need is to be led to fortune through humility. This must be cultivated through the offspring. This is what the Ashram is for.
Ask yourselves if you are living in a manner worthy of upholding God's justice.
Due to the lack of good innate tendencies, no matter how highly one can think, emotions will still accompany it.
You only need to think about what to do with the time you get and how to utilize it. Both actions and thoughts will bear fruit. Wealth may be less, but prosperity will be abundant.
It is easy to speak of truth, kindness, and compassion. But do we have a karma in our hands to unify all these?
The wise are those who advise by perceiving the past, present, and future.
No deity is of any consequence before a wise person. The various conditions assumed by the body can only be understood through the evolution of this soul.
In our lifetime, we may only be able to see one or two self-realized souls (Atmajnanis).

That is, we must have a certain determination: I will achieve it, I must achieve it. What is primarily needed for this is a walking stick. Or rather, a resolve; that stick of resolve must be kept from breaking.
You must have a perfect awareness of the example you are to set for the world.
Both men and women must take care not to corrupt their imagination so that mind, word, and deed may reach their goal.
Pournami is the fulfillment of the purity of intention across multiple births, acted upon knowingly or unknowingly.
The fruit of Pournami prayer is so supremely excellent that it cannot be diminished by anything else.
The Pournami vow yields the combined benefits of all other vows.
Pournami is a day of glory in every respect.
Observing a vow on Pournami is primarily for the purification of ancestors.
We must guard our minds. In all living beings, its respective mind imparts its nature.
If a dual mind arises, you will be unable to act there.
Looking at the sky, it appears empty. But how many things exist there! Let the mind be as vast as the sky and the ocean.
Imagination arises according to each individual's innate tendencies. It is the tendency of the soul.
From the time of creation, the world has existed with both good and evil.
The world is always functioning in such a way that both good and bad are churned together so that we can extract its essence.
Through what did the existence of the world come about?
In this world, whether it be great souls or other living beings, no two are alike. That is the glory of God.
In this nature, everything has been endowed with its own love, respect, devotion, and humility. Everyone demonstrates this difference in knowledge.
There is knowledge. There is meaning in what is known. Sannyasins are those who have attained both.
'Experience must be first and foremost' – this has a very profound meaning.
Experience means realizing through perception in the states described by the great sages as Jagrat (waking), Svapna (dreaming), Sushupti (deep sleep), Turiya, and Turiyatita.
Experience is what is needed first. If someone goes out to discover it, we must advance by holding onto what has been discovered.
It is your experience that bears witness to you. That will subsequently translate into action.
Our primary asset is experience. The beginning will be difficult. According to the level of sincerity, the difficulty will pass.
We are experiencing the remnants of karma that pervade the world as virtues and sins.
Receiving a divine voice means becoming qualified to be a guide for the world.
Know that experiential knowledge is more authoritative than hearsay.
Most of us have a tendency not to stay when we see something good. The reason for this is a lack of precedent in seeing, hearing, and familiarizing ourselves with good things.
As long as the truth is not seen fully, experience remains incomplete.
In this nature, everything has been endowed with its respective love, respect, devotion, humility, and knowledge.
See the earth as a bed of flowers.
There is a measure of the light of Brahman for the movement of the solar system.
This atmosphere consists of the spheres of influence of so many Yuga Dharmas and the five elements.
Just like the gravitational field between the earth and the solar system, there is a gravitational field among these stars as well.
Changes in the nature of the sky occur just as the epochs of each Manu change.
There are certain realms capable of attracting and holding not just our actions but our very earth itself.
This earth possesses a cosmic truth. It has a special power.
Nature has been proving to us over time that this is also a warning: 'Do not forget the truth.'
The Sun, the Moon, and the Earth stand within the protective sphere of the nine planets.

The aspects of the gross, the subtle, the cause, and the effect are intertwined with the attributes of the soul's Karma and Dharma. The Guru who validates the soul's Karma and Dharma attributes alongside the gross, subtle, cause, and effect must be an action-oriented hero of experiential wisdom who acts respecting the five elements, the five senses, the five sheaths, the Jivatma, the Paramatma, and the course of Dharma.
Nature possesses a far-reaching knowledge. You can understand everything from this knowledge that stands both near and far.
In this world, from every grain of sand to whatever things arise and perish, everything has its own wholeness.
From whichever transcendent peak the Veda originated. That is, light originated, knowledge originated. That is a special ordinance of Brahman.
This atmosphere is filled with the atoms of complete expressions. Every word, every glance, and every expression of ours will transfer and linger in this atmosphere.

If you take a long look into this atmosphere, you can see how many atoms twinkle and vanish within the circumference of a single rupee coin. It is enough to think that we are just one among such countless atoms.
Our erosion of values is due to the fact that, by God's resolve or Brahman's resolve, we failed to gain the realization that Ishvara, God, Brahman, and Parabrahman are all distinctly different.
The action coming from me, a woman, must correct the mistakes of women in this world, and men too must think in this way; that should be your qualification.
The deer and the rabbit are the most tender creatures. Most women have a heart like that of a rabbit.
The woman is the primary pillar of a home. Being this core element, she must inherently possess a certain nobility.

Guiding even a single woman towards wisdom will elevate a household. Her subsequent generation will also flourish. If this is done as an offering to the Divine, this sown seed will proliferate throughout the entire world.
It is women who perform duties more gracefully and with greater understanding than men do.
If one is not vigilant, inner forces can undermine the purity of a woman's character during her menstrual period.
A woman inherently possesses nine vital facets (kalas), which must be fully actualized in practice.

A woman radiating prosperity (*Shree*) must evolve across both gross and subtle realms; manifesting as the universal truth of a mother, the grace of divinity, and the primordial guru who reveals the inner spiritual guide as the ultimate embodiment of truth.

Most girls today grow up devoid of any contemplation regarding where they were born, or the profound purpose behind their birth and upbringing. They exhibit a sheer tendency to merely adorn themselves and wander aimlessly, lacking the drive to accomplish anything significant or inspire others to do so.
Observing the topography of Kerala, it appears as an eternal spring.
Even the sages ardently prayed to the Divine, pleading for a birth that would allow them to witness the *Kali Yuga*. Furthermore, they desired that this birth must specifically occur in Bharat.
Bharat is a profoundly evolved land. It serves as the fertile ground for diverse lineages of sages and supreme spiritual wisdom.
The children of Bharat are fundamentally one, regardless of their diverse affiliations.
We Indians have degraded to such an extent that it has induced alterations even within the natural world.
Each and every individual must ask themselves: 'To what extent have I contributed to my home, my nation, and ultimately, to the entire world?'
Bharat is a naturally endowed land. Our culture possesses an unfathomable depth. Our profound knowledge has been lost precisely because we have failed to structure our lives in alignment with it.
Indian culture is the most supreme in the world. No other nation possesses such a magnificent cultural heritage.
If the culture and heritage of India fail to flourish and strengthen, the very existence of the world will be imperiled.

A distinct virtue of India is that numerous sages emerged here as profound visionaries. India will never initiate an unprovoked attack on any nation. This non-aggression is an integral aspect of this virtue, serving as the very foundation of Indian culture.
Where were we born? Where were we nurtured? What is the profound majesty of our native landscape? We remain entirely unprepared to reflect upon any of these fundamental questions.
An individual who lacks proficiency in at least one language is deprived of the opportunity to learn anything else.
Ultimately, if individuals lack profound proficiency in their native tongue, they inevitably fail to cultivate a genuine love for the language.
Among the various months that harmonize with the rituals and ethos of this land, the month of *Chingam* is uniquely auspicious in every respect.
Out of the twenty-seven asterisms in the month of *Chingam*, the *Chothi* star holds a particularly distinguished significance.

Resembling the unpredictable trajectory of a blazing fire—twisting, turning, sprinting, and singing—we collectively liberate ourselves from inescapable entanglements. Such is the defining nature of this current epoch.
There is no epoch quite like the *Kali Yuga*, a time wherein relentless effort and arduous labor can manifest any desired outcome into reality.

We must consciously adapt to the changing times, as time itself will certainly not alter its course for our convenience. Given that the current epoch is the *Kali Yuga*, the propagation of *Dharma* must be meticulously tailored to suit its specific characteristics.
The Divine holds both specific stature and designated temporal domains. The quintessential eras of the Divine are the *Treta Yuga* and the *Dwapara Yuga*.
What defines the intrinsic nature of this current epoch? It is profoundly corrupted, permeated by a pervasive demonic disposition.

The *Kali Yuga* does not denote absolute annihilation. The four *Varnas* (social orders) remain eternally present. It is the paramount importance of character refinement that the *Brahmana*, *Kshatriya*, *Vaishya*, and *Shudra* must fundamentally comprehend.
*Sanatana* represents the cumulative cultural and spiritual wisdom imparted by the eminent Gurus of respective eras; it is an enduring cultural framework perpetually applicable across time.
We seldom contemplate the profound depths of our magnificent cultural heritage, failing to recognize that profound humility is its defining hallmark.
The unadulterated truth of history resides in a dimension far transcending even the concept of divine stature.

Ironically, even to scholars versed in philosophy, our profound cultural narratives are often reduced to mere mythological tales, while Western narratives are universally esteemed as authentic history.
The very earth inhabited by a human being capable of perceiving the innate goodness of the Divine will be invariably transformed by the radiance of his own inherent goodness.

Regarding the linguistic heritage of Kerala, it can arguably be classified as one of the most expansive languages. There exists no other language endowed with such an extensive array of phonetic characters.
Ultimately, the entire global populace will be compelled to embrace both the language of Kerala and the foundational *Dharma* of India.
Only the one who inherently possesses can truly give; merely the one who has attained profound knowledge can enlighten others.
Whatever subject one chooses to contemplate, one must immerse in it completely, granting the subject absolute conceptual completeness in thought.

The immutable law of nature dictates a journey of ultimate perfection, where the life force, originating from a subatomic particle and progressively evolving through myriad animate and inanimate forms—from a blade of grass to a rudimentary worm—eventually attains profound union with the Supreme Soul.
The very thoughts that emanate from our consciousness will ultimately envelop and govern our entire being.
Much like meticulously discerning subtle variations within a single color palette, we can critically analyze and delineate the intricate nuances of our own thoughts and deliberations.

If we passively absorb the distorted historical narratives regurgitated by a marginal group of individuals—who senselessly propagate superficial rationalism and empty theories of liberation utterly disconnected from genuine sacrifice—how far can we conceivably progress?

Observing the contemporary turbulence within the political sphere evokes a stark comparison: it is akin to scooping a mere pitcher of water from the vast ocean and presumptuously declaring it to be the ocean itself.
Mahatma Gandhi adamantly anchored his ideology to the reverence of Rama and the utopian vision of *Ramarajya*. Historically and practically, this clinging was a profound miscalculation on his part.

Are not the figures of Rama and the utopian paradigm of *Ramarajya* inherently bound to the *Treta Yuga*, rendering them utterly obsolete in the context of our contemporary *Yugadharma* (the ethos of the current epoch)?
The superficial semblance of independent thought prevalent in the nation today is, in reality, a residual artifact of the protracted British colonial administration.
The authentic indigenous heritage must be meticulously cultivated and elevated for the prosperity of both our homes and our nation; not the imposed cultural legacy of the West.
True administrative authority is fundamentally derived from the profound merit accrued through genuine humility, righteous action, and unwavering adherence to *Dharma*.

Every ostensibly beneficial provision that has historically descended from the centralized state apparatus represents, in truth, a destructive trajectory destined to ruin both the populace and the wider world.

The modern state apparatus embodies a profound ignorance, systematically betraying the public by manipulating national interests to appease divisive factions of caste and religion for transient, opportunistic gains.

Within Bharat, contemporary political administrators pathetically grovel at the feet of a prominent Vedic orthodoxy—an establishment obsessed with ritualistic offerings and displays of dominance—crying out in despair, "Oh Lord, we possess no salvation; please save us!"

Utterly suffocated by the oppressive direct rule of historical monarchies and feudal lords, divisive forces of caste and religion intensified to extreme levels, reducing the collective public life to a near-moribund state. Although superficial actions may masquerade as independent thought, the populace remains thoroughly alienated from locating their authentic, traditional existential roots.

The essential ideological shift required is to transform governance into a deeply sanctified process—one fundamentally grounded in genuine humility, righteous action, unwavering *Dharma*, and absolute spiritual merit.

The overarching state apparatus intrinsically encompasses diverse entities: the believer and the cynic, the devout and the atheist, the ignorant fool and the social outcast. It must invariably possess the intrinsic capability to effectively guide and realign the populace according to the specific necessities of their temporal epoch.

A *Shudra* inherently possesses the unalienable right to govern. This fundamental prerogative existed throughout all historical epochs; the restrictive assertion denying this right is a deceptive fabrication inscribed in later eras.

A profound, systemic traditional failure has emerged primarily because timeless, universally applicable philosophical concepts were never systematically disseminated to the populace as actionable knowledge through the governing institutions.

Through ceaseless political manipulations and systemic machinations within the state apparatus, consecutive governments have extensively sown the very seeds of destruction, leaving the hapless citizens to reap the catastrophic harvest. Furthermore, academic historians submissively tread this identical path, utterly failing to enlighten the masses regarding these profound detriments.

Historically, we have consistently been subjected to governments utterly bereft of the essential wisdom of proper conduct toward the citizenry. Irrespective of the magnitude of the regime in power, each has systematically engaged in institutionalized corruption and deceit. Consequently, what exemplary model remains for us to emulate and guide our existence?
To have attained a human birth within the sacred expanse of India is the manifestation of the highest possible spiritual merit.
The inviolable dictate of *Dharma* proclaims that a state apparatus can only achieve true righteousness if it is firmly undergirded by the profound blessings of an enlightened ascetic.
The contemporary political leadership consists entirely of individuals who completely lack a fundamental comprehension of the profound inner essence that defines authentic Indian civilization.
Profound peril inherently lurks within romantic passions that remain devoid of the critical discernment between virtuous and destructive forces.
We are currently consumed by an insatiable eagerness to consolidate authoritative power through the blind adoption of an English-centric model of existence.

Individuals who completely succumbed to adopting the linguistic and sartorial customs of the West invariably deteriorated morally. How profoundly degraded we ourselves must be, as we eagerly invite this epicenter of arrogance into our lives and clamor to extol it as a superior standard.

Can contemporary modern philosophy secure true emancipation from mental subjugation? Such instantaneous liberation is fundamentally impossible through these superficial frameworks. True liberation can only be attained through profound spirituality, or a deep comprehension of the subtle realms of existence.

While the Western populace pragmatically tailored their attire in accordance with their distinct geographical climatic realities, we foolishly imitated them devoid of any critical thought. Numerous great sages have articulated this critique; yet, you stubbornly refused to acknowledge it. We remain chronically obsessed with eagerly validating and adopting whatever the Western world exhibits or dictates.

We have indiscriminately consumed both the virtues and the profound vices of Western culture, engaging in comprehensive mimicry across every conceivable level. Ironically, when the spiritually destitute Westerner arrived upon our shores seeking solace and adopted ascetic practices like growing long hair, even the most ordinary local laborers and boatmen absurdly began imitating this superficial gesture.

Everyone functions like a compass pointing towards the West. Apart from regurgitating what is taught and passing examinations, what do we possess that is truly our own? We are inclined to look either towards the West or the North.

When we hear the word 'Ashram', our assumption is that it is a place for renunciation (*sannyasa*). Isn't Shantiniketan an ashram? Are children enrolled there to become ascetics? Even Sree Krishna lived in the ashram of Sage Sandipani. Was Sree Krishna sent there to become an ascetic? There are also those who believe that one should not go to an ashram at all.
Coming to an ashram, believing in it, and residing there is not for renunciation. It is to learn through life.

Through the ashram and the learning acquired there, whatever deficiencies exist in our homes are resolved and fulfilled through our intellect, hardship, sacrifice, and action (*karma*). This is the spiritual knowledge (*atmavidya*) acquired from the ashram; it is not renunciation.

'Aaa...shramam' signifies earnest effort. The core essence of every ashram is to impart love, respect, and humility, functioning in a way that brings goodness to the world. That is the education gained from an ashram. Merely claiming that one has been to an ashram, studied the Vedas, learned Vedanta, or acquired skills in music and arts is of no real consequence. All these aforementioned things can be obtained anywhere.

You should never lead an ashram life solely looking at the goodness of the ashram. You must also envision your own well-being alongside it. If you do not prioritize your own betterment, none of this will materialize. Any reformation should be in a manner that engenders goodness within us.
The discipline of the ashram deeply touching one's inner self is also a profound experience (*anubhuthi*).
When referring to an ashram, it must have an underlying ideal or philosophy.

Women should not enter an ashram. This is your understanding. How did this ignorance come upon you? You have not realized that this is the remnant of a traditional practice that prohibited women from having education, wealth, and authority, and even forbade them from wearing proper clothing. Those who taught history also imparted it in this exact manner.
Is any place accorded to culture here? Living like this, how much can you truly comprehend the concept of an ashram?
This ashram is a realm of spiritual experience.
What is achieved through a hundred lifetimes can be attained in a single lifetime through familiarity with the ashram.
No one has ever reformed the entire world in one single stroke.

To showcase the sacrifice of Mahatmaji, a true renunciate is required. Even after enduring kicks from soldiers, that man did not consider it a major issue, but rather demonstrated what the richness of sacrifice truly is. How have we perceived even that profound sacrifice? A subsequent generation capable of upholding his steadfast detachment never evolved. That became a tragedy. Neither a community of followers nor a government stepped forward to illustrate to us the history of that contemporary sacrifice.
If freedom is obtained as though through forceful seizure, it will not be conducive to our living without discrimination.
We are not a people who have attained a freedom that enables us to live without differences.
Each of us has fallen and decayed into a course of action (*karmagathi*) that respects nothing and no one, akin to gathering worthless dregs after extracting the essence.

Each one of you is a wealthy person in your day-to-day life. His loss, profit, undermining the roots of the working class. Undermining the roots of the capitalist by exacting wages without doing work. This is the only knowledge the world has imparted to us.
Ayurveda is the Veda that safeguards the secret of longevity. Among the guidelines shown to us by our ancestors, Ayurveda is one of the most important.
The unique ideology, path, and medium of Santhigiri is to empower people to transcend caste and religion and arrive at the unified principle of humanity.

What is established in Santhigiri is the symbol of a karmic vision aimed at guiding not only spiritual thinkers but also seekers and even ordinary people onto the path of wisdom, thereby transforming them into embodiments of Dharma.

The objective of the ashram is the goal achieved by nurturing individuals in the realm of spiritual vision, guiding them through various states of transformation, and enabling them to act in accordance with the will of the Brahman.
Santhigiri's path is one of knowledge, which observes and listens to the mistakes of the past.
The action (*karma*) at Santhigiri is a return to castelessness.
The message of Santhigiri is an unwavering karmic fortitude that serves the creations of the world and aids in the resolution of unintended consequences incurred along the path of life.
The ashram life at Santhigiri is one that untangles every knot accumulated over past lifetimes.
The path at Santhigiri is the divine resolve (*Brahmanischayam*). It is this path that is called Sanatana.

The ideology of Santhigiri is not a religious dharma. It is an action (*karma*) aimed at articulating the errors that have occurred among the people, correcting those mistakes, and enabling the people to come forward.

The endeavor taking place at Santhigiri involves evaluating and understanding everything that has transpired to date, removing the flaws within, systematizing it according to the times, shaping the impending future state, and bringing it to the forefront.
The knowledge of Santhigiri is one guided by God. This is the knowledge bestowed upon us as the Supreme Brahman.
A karmic potency erupts from here in a manner that makes the world understand what the mission of Santhigiri truly is.
What occurs at Santhigiri is a path of karmic resolution capable of functioning and enabling others to function beneficially for all living beings in the world.
The message of Santhigiri will forever stand as a truth of Dharma functioning according to the will of the Brahman, like the abounding merit of the dawn.
Human life, which constantly practices Karma and Dharma and becomes the symbol of the absolute right to Karma and Dharma, is entitled even to liberation (*Mukti*). This is the vision of Santhigiri.
I have neither education nor wealth. However, the knowledge present here is one step ahead of all the knowledge in the world.
God has a purpose in having created the character of our ashram in this manner.
The goal of Santhigiri is to impart and fulfill the merits of the respective eras of the fourteen Manus known as the Manu lineage.
The prayer of Santhigiri is the prayer given by God to rectify all the diverse kinds of householders (*Grihasthashramis*) and all the various shortcomings that exist in the world.
The good will be sustained by the good, and the bad will be destroyed by the bad. This is the realization of the vision! The divine resolve of Santhigiri! Or rather, ordained by the Brahman!!
Once education, wealth, and authority are equally attained, human endeavor is then directed toward peace. 'Peace and harmony for the world'—this is the Dharma of Santhigiri.
There is absolutely no doubt that peace and harmony will be achieved in the world.
Our aim is to provide peace and harmony to the world.
The jurisprudence of Dharma (*Dharmaneethi Shastra*) of Santhigiri is a providential care intended to cultivate a life of Dharma by obeying and fostering obedience to divine justice.

Within 30 years in India, certain prominent political figures and people of *Sattvic* nature will come together to hoist a flag of peace. Towards that end, all of us believers, without distinctions of class or religion, and without languishing in the perils of the prevailing *Varnashrama Dharma*, must stand united as intelligent children, shoulder to shoulder, and raise a national organization infused with genuine devotion to God and humility. Through this, the intellect and strength of the people will emerge even more vigorous and robust.

The Word is Truth
Truth is Guru
Guru is God
—this disembodied voice must be revered, worshipped, and honored.
The Santhigiri Ashram, where the holy waters of religion-transcending spirituality ripple.

In 1969, Navajyothi Karunakara Guru established the Santhigiri Ashram centered at Pothencode in Thiruvananthapuram district. The ashram operates with the intent of leading humanity toward the goal of human progress through material and spiritual purity of action (*karmashudhi*). The ashram propagates the principles of human liberation: *Annadanam* (offering food), *Athurasevanam* (caring for the sick), and *Athmabodhanam* (spiritual awakening). Material and spiritual causes and effects are complementary in connecting humanity and nature. The objective of the ashram is the exploration into the realms of meaning in a religion-transcending spirituality grounded in the purity of action. The pilgrimages into the unseen dimensions of universal peace are mantras for human liberation. They are also the philosophical code of existence.

The experiential doctrine of divine providence, which has traversed all sanctums, stands as the divine resolve (*Brahmanischayam*), serving as the supreme merit of the Dharma of the age (*Yugadharma*).
